assumptions.condition: The coordinates \(U_i\), \(i\in\mathbb Z\), are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
The graph rule is translation equivariant: \(G(\theta^kU)=\theta^kG(U)\) for every \(k\in\mathbb Z\).
The set of edges of \(G\) incident to \(i\) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(U_{i-r},\ldots,U_{i+r})\).
Every neighbor of \(i\) in \(G\) belongs to \(\{i-r,\ldots,i+r\}\).
The exposure maps satisfy \(E_{i+k}(\theta^kd,\theta^kG)=E_i(d,G)\) for every \(i,k\in\mathbb Z\) and assignment \(d\).
The common potential-outcome schedule satisfies \(Y_{i+k}(\theta^kd;\theta^kU,\theta^kG)=Y_i(d;U,G)\) for every \(i,k\in\mathbb Z\) and assignment \(d\).
For every assignment \(d\), the pair \(E_i(d,G),Y_i(d;U,G)\) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(U_j,d_j:i-r\le j\le i+r)\).
The common envelope \(|Y_i(d;U,G)|\le B\) holds \(P\)-almost surely for every \(i\in\mathbb Z\) and assignment \(d\).
Conditional on \(\mathcal F_U\), the coordinates of each \(D^{(w)}\), \(w\in\{1,2\}\), are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) draws under \(P\).
The assignment fields \(D^{(1)}\) and \(D^{(2)}\) are conditionally independent given \(\mathcal F_U\) under \(P\).

novel.justification: Large online populations can be rerandomized after a prespecified washout interval while retaining the same network, eligibility frame, exposure map, and potential-outcome schedule; the condition formalizes that repeated-experiment design.

assumptions.condition: The exposure propensities obey \(\min\{\pi_i(e_1),\pi_i(e_0)\}\ge\varepsilon\) \(P\)-almost surely for every \(i\in\mathbb Z\).

definitions.name: Two-wave finite-range Palm exposure class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}:=\{P:(U_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}\text{ is iid};\ G\text{ is shift equivariant and radius-}r\text{ local};\ E_i\text{ and }Y_i\text{ are shift equivariant and radius-}r\text{ local};\ |Y_i(d;U,G)|\le B;\ D^{(1)}\text{ and }D^{(2)}\text{ are conditionally independent given }\mathcal F_U;\ D_i^{(w)}\mid\mathcal F_U\text{ are iid }\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p);\ \min_{a\in\{e_1,e_0\}}\pi_i(a)\ge\varepsilon\text{ for every }i\in\mathbb Z\}\).

definitions.name: Wavewise design--population score decomposition
definitions.construction: For \(w\in\{1,2\}\), \(Z_i^{(w)}-\tau_{\mathrm P}=\xi_i^{(w)}+h_i\), where \(m_i=\mathbb E_P[Z_i^{(w)}\mid\mathcal F_U]\), \(\xi_i^{(w)}=Z_i^{(w)}-m_i\), and \(h_i=m_i-\tau_{\mathrm P}\).

definitions.name: Buffered F\o lner restriction
definitions.construction: For each \(n>4r\), restrict the infinite construction to \(\Lambda_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), run both randomization waves on \(\Lambda_n\), discard \(\Lambda_n\setminus I_n\), and retain \(Z_{n,i}^{(w)}\) for \(i\in I_n\) and \(w\in\{1,2\}\).

definitions.name: Observable two-wave population-variance statistic
definitions.construction: Compute \(\widehat\tau_n^{(w)}=N_n^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_n}Z_{n,i}^{(w)}\) for \(w\in\{1,2\}\), then set \(\widehat\Omega_n^{12}=\sum_{k=-2r}^{2r}\{N_{n,k}^{-1}\sum_{i\in J_{n,k}}Z_{n,i}^{(1)}Z_{n,i+k}^{(2)}-\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}\widehat\tau_n^{(2)}\}\). The only nuisance quantities are the two displayed wave means; \(p\) and \(\pi_i(a)\) are known from the randomization.

definitions.name: Zero and positive population-variance witnesses
definitions.construction: Let \(U_i\) be independent Rademacher variables, let \(G\) be the deterministic nearest-neighbor line, take \(E_i(d,G)=d_i\), \(e_1=1\), \(e_0=0\), and define \(P^{\Delta}\) by \(Y_i(d;U,G)=(U_i-U_{i-1})d_i\) and \(P^{+}\) by \(Y_i(d;U,G)=U_id_i\), with the two assignment waves drawn independently at probability \(p\).

definitions.name: Minimax-rate handle
definitions.construction: Determine the sharp two-wave testing radius by pairing a Le Cam two-point lower-bound family of bounded noisy radius-one outcome schedules with higher-order cross-wave degenerate statistics that exploit the Janson coboundary restriction under \(H_0\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\), \(n>4r\), \(i\in I_n\), and \(w\in\{1,2\}\), the restriction coupling satisfies \(Z_{n,i}^{(w)}=Z_i^{(w)}\) almost surely, and \(|\Lambda_n\setminus I_n|/|\Lambda_n|=2r/n\to0\).
statements.justification: The exact interior coupling makes one buffered F\o lner sequence the sole finite-to-infinite-volume regime.
statements.gap: BaryshnikovYukich2005 studies stabilizing finite-volume scores, while this proposition records the boundary deletion for two repeated exposure experiments on a fixed local graph.
statements.consumer: An online experimenter can implement the diagnostic after dropping a prespecified fixed-width endpoint buffer.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\), \(Z_i^{(w)}-\tau_{\mathrm P}=\xi_i^{(w)}+h_i\) and \(\mathbb E_P[\xi_i^{(w)}h_j]=0\) for all \(i,j\in\mathbb Z\) and \(w\in\{1,2\}\). In addition, \(|Z_i^{(w)}|\le K\) almost surely.
statements.justification: The decomposition retains the sound assignment--environment split and supplies the common envelope required for a uniform diagnostic.
statements.gap: AbadieAtheyImbensWooldridge2020 separates sampling and design uncertainty without repeated local exposure-IPW scores; Leung2022ANI works conditionally on one realized finite population.
statements.consumer: The split identifies which cross-wave products eliminate assignment noise and which envelope controls finite-sample error.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\) and \(i,j\in\mathbb Z\), \(\mathbb E_P[Z_i^{(1)}Z_j^{(2)}\mid\mathcal F_U]=m_im_j\) almost surely. Therefore \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=\sum_{k=-2r}^{2r}\{\mathbb E_P[Z_0^{(1)}Z_k^{(2)}]-\tau_{\mathrm P}^2\}\).
statements.justification: Conditional replication converts the latent population covariance into an observable cross-wave moment without estimating \(m_i\).
statements.gap: AronowSamii2017 identifies exposure means within one randomization, while this lemma identifies the superpopulation covariance component by two conditionally independent waves.
statements.consumer: The identity lets a platform estimate graph-to-graph exposure-effect variation using only recorded assignments, exposures, outcomes, and known propensities.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\), the process \(h_i\) is a centered \((2r+1)\)-block factor and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\ge0\). The equality \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\) holds if and only if a square-integrable \(2r\)-block factor \(g_i\) satisfies \(h_i=g_i-g_{i-1}\) almost surely; in that case \(N_n^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_n}h_i=(g_{n-r}-g_r)/N_n\), and \(\sum_{i\in I_n}h_i\Rightarrow g^\star-g_0\).
statements.justification: This cited corollary interprets the diagnostic null as the known finite-block coboundary boundary rather than as causal homogeneity.
statements.gap: Janson2015, Theorems 1--2 and Corollary 1 already establish the finite-dependent coboundary and endpoint laws; this proposition only specializes that published substrate to the declared score notation.
statements.consumer: A researcher who fails to reject can report the correct boundary interpretation without claiming that unit-level exposure effects are constant.

statements.justification: The explicit uniform deviation inequality is the load-bearing result that turns the latent Janson boundary into a finite-sample observable object.
statements.gap: Janson2015 classifies zero long-run variance but supplies no test from randomized causal scores; FanLengWu2025 estimates the asymptotic variance of a regression-adjusted direct-effect estimator under a low-rank graphon model and does not give this two-wave finite-sample bound.
statements.consumer: Repeated online experiments obtain a prespecified, regression-free error bar for the population component even when the null lies on a degenerate coboundary boundary.

statements.statement: For every \(n>4r\), the test \(\phi_{n,\alpha}\) satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}:\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0}P(\phi_{n,\alpha}=1)\le\alpha\). For every \(\beta\in(0,1)\), it also satisfies \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}:\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\ge\rho_n(\alpha,\beta)}P(\phi_{n,\alpha}=1)\ge1-\beta\), where \(\rho_n(\alpha,\beta)=2b_n+q_n(\alpha)+q_n(\beta)=O(n^{-1/2})\) for fixed \(r,B,\varepsilon,\alpha,\beta\).
statements.justification: This theorem gives the requested operational boundary diagnostic, a nonasymptotic size guarantee, and a derived attainable separation rate over one exact class.
statements.gap: Leung2022ANI gives fixed-population network-HAC inference from one assignment, and FanLengWu2025 gives low-rank-graphon variance inference for a regression-adjusted average direct effect; neither tests whether a Palm exposure-score covariance is zero using repeated assignments.
statements.consumer: A platform with two washout-separated waves can decide whether population generalization requires a network-population variance component before reporting its exposure effect.

statements.statement: If \(B\ge2\) and \(\varepsilon\le\min\{p,1-p\}\), then \(P^{\Delta},P^{+}\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\) with \(r=1\). Under \(P^{\Delta}\), \(h_i=U_i-U_{i-1}\) and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\); under \(P^{+}\), \(h_i=U_i\) and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=1\).
statements.justification: The paired laws verify that the null contains heterogeneous effects and that the alternative class is nonempty under one common envelope.
statements.gap: LiWager2022 discusses assignment-dominated limits in a dense graphon setting; these radius-one line examples isolate cancellation and positive Palm variation in the exact class used by the diagnostic.
statements.consumer: The two laws provide finite-range simulation benchmarks for checking rejection frequencies and power calculations.

statements.statement: What is the minimax separation rate for testing \(H_0:\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\) against \(H_1:\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\ge s_n\) from two waves over \(\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\)? In particular, determine whether the attainable order \(s_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\) in the size--separation theorem is sharp or whether a statistic exploiting the coboundary degeneracy can separate a strictly smaller order while retaining uniform level \(\alpha\).
statements.justification: The attainable root-sample-size rate need not be optimal at a quadratic, degenerate null, so the sharp testing frontier remains substantive open content.
statements.gap: Janson2015 characterizes the null algebraically but gives no statistical experiment or minimax testing result; the network-interference papers cited here do not study this boundary-testing problem.
statements.consumer: A sharp lower or faster upper rate would determine the number of users and repeated assignments required to certify negligible population variation.

sampling_model.design: Two conditionally independent Bernoulli assignment waves with known probability \(p\) are run on the same finite interval \(\Lambda_n\), with a prespecified washout and a fixed-width interior buffer.
sampling_model.units: One realization of a stationary radius-\(r\) innovation network on \(\mathbb Z\), observed through \(\Lambda_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and analyzed on \(I_n\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary assignments \(D_i^{(1)}\) and \(D_i^{(2)}\) enter the same local exposure maps and no-carryover potential-outcome schedule.
sampling_model.overlap: Both focal exposures have conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\) in each wave.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The propensities are known from the design. The statistic estimates only the two wave means \(\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat\tau_n^{(2)}\); it does not estimate \(m_i\) or fit a regression.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 and Corollary 1 show that zero asymptotic variance for a stationary finite-variance finite-dependent sequence is equivalent to a finite-dependent coboundary and yields an unnormalized endpoint-difference law.
The paper proves consistency and asymptotic normality for exposure-IPW estimators under approximate neighborhood interference and studies network-HAC inference for one randomized finite population.
The paper proves central limit and invariance principles for stationary fields represented as functions of independent innovations under short-range physical dependence.
The paper proves treatment-effect asymptotics under graphon-random interference and develops direct- and indirect-effect inference.

The preprint proves asymptotic normality and optimality for regression-adjusted average-direct-effect estimators under graphon interference and consistently estimates the linear estimator's asymptotic variance under a low-rank graphon condition.

tldr: Two independent assignment waves on one buffered F\o lner interval turn the latent Palm population covariance into an observable cross-wave IPW moment. The statistic \(\widehat\Omega_n^{12}\) uses only the two wave scores and their sample means, obeys an explicit uniform finite-sample concentration inequality, and yields a level-\(\alpha\) test of \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\) with uniformly guaranteed power at the derived \(n^{-1/2}\) separation scale. Janson2015 supplies the finite-block coboundary and endpoint law as known substrate; the theorem-level contribution is the repeated-randomization diagnostic, not a causal relabeling of that probability result.

project_justification.gap: Janson2015 exactly classifies the zero-long-run-variance boundary for finite block factors, while existing network-interference papers analyze effect estimation or variance estimation from one randomization. None supplies an observable, uniformly size-controlled test of whether the Palm population component itself vanishes.
project_justification.niche: Repeated online randomization on the same local network makes cross-wave IPW products conditionally remove assignment noise, converting the latent boundary into a directly estimable finite-lag functional.
project_justification.fill: The project defines the complete two-wave statistic and nuisance means, proves an explicit concentration inequality, derives finite-sample size and power guarantees at an attainable root-sample-size separation, and leaves only the sharp minimax rate as open content.

related_work: Janson2015 is the primary mathematical comparator. Its Theorems 1--2 and Corollary 1 already give the finite-dependent zero-variance, block-factor coboundary, and endpoint-difference laws, so those results enter only as cited substrate for interpreting the null. Leung2022ANI supplies the one-wave exposure-IPW framework and approximate-neighborhood-interference perspective, but its finite-population target and network-HAC estimator differ from the two-wave Palm population-variance diagnostic. AronowSamii2017 supplies the exposure-mapping and known-propensity design foundation, not a repeated-wave population-covariance test. ElMachkouriVolnyWu2013 informs the iid-innovation representation; no new central limit theorem is claimed against it. LiWager2022 studies direct and indirect effects under a generally dense graphon-random model, whereas the diagnostic here uses a fixed-radius sparse local score and two assignments on the same realized environment. FanLengWu2025 uses a possibly sparse graphon, restricts its consistent linear-estimator variance formula to a low-rank graphon, targets the average direct effect, and estimates the asymptotic variance of its regression-adjusted estimator. The present target is instead the zero boundary of the Palm covariance component of a local exposure-IPW score, and its estimator is the regression-free cross-wave covariance statistic \(\widehat\Omega_n^{12}\).
technical_internal_limitation: The design requires two conditionally independent assignment waves applied to the same no-carryover potential-outcome schedule. The single-wave BondEtAl2012 experiment cannot be reanalyzed with this diagnostic. The finite-radius restriction and ambient interval lags are deliberate: the proposal does not assert approximate-neighborhood-interference transfer, random-radius stabilization, graph-distance HAC consistency, or unchanged-HAC exactness.
honest_scope: The observable cross-wave identity, uniform concentration bound, and size--power theorem are the proposed results. Janson's finite-block coboundary and endpoint law are published inputs and carry no novelty claim. The minimax optimality of the derived \(n^{-1/2}\) separation rate remains open. As a cited sanity check, homogeneous conditional effects give \(h_i=0\) and lie on the zero side, consistent with assignment-dominated cases discussed by LiWager2022; Proposition 3 shows that homogeneity is not necessary.
novelty_justification: Janson2015 makes the latent zero-variance boundary mathematically explicit but does not make it statistically observable in a randomized causal experiment. The proposed field contribution is the two-wave cross-randomization identity and its finite-sample uniformly valid diagnostic, including a fully specified statistic, nuisance means, threshold, and attainable separation radius. No graph-HAC, random-metric, block-factor coboundary, endpoint-law, or generic central-limit novelty is claimed.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic: Observable two-wave diagnostic for Palm population variance under exact finite-range local interference. Under bounded local exposure outcomes and two conditionally independent Bernoulli assignment waves sharing one no-carryover schedule, identify Ω_pop by cross-wave IPW moments; prove uniform finite-sample concentration, size and power, an exactly unbiased lag-separated diagnostic, and a sharp root-n score-vector minimax rate at balanced assignment. Janson’s coboundary result is cited substrate. No ANI transfer, endogenous graph-distance HAC, annealed CLT/Wald theorem, or Bond-et-al. reanalysis is claimed.

message: Rebuilt the kernel around an explicit two-wave IPW diagnostic with finite-sample size control and an attainable root-n separation rate; treated Janson's coboundary/endpoint law as cited substrate. Proposal gate and rendered-LaTeX compilation pass.
